media_work.title: 60 Minutes
media_work.focus_or_theme: False confessions, police interrogation techniques, juvenile suspects, wrongful convictions in Chicago.
media_work.summaryNotes: Chicago identified as having a high number of documented false confession cases ("False Confession Capital").

media_item.focus_or_theme: False confessions, police interrogation techniques, juvenile suspects, wrongful convictions in Chicago.
media_item.summary_notes: This 60 Minutes segment focuses on false confessions, police interrogation techniques, and wrongful convictions, particularly in Chicago. It highlights the psychological vulnerability of suspects during interrogation and the potential for police tactics to induce false confessions.
key_quotes_raw: Interviews with exonerated individuals describing interrogation experiences
Psychologist Saul Kassin explaining the psychology of false confessions
Cook County State's Attorney Anita Alvarez defending police actions at the time
systemic_issues_raw: Psychological vulnerability of suspects (especially juveniles) during intense interrogation
Police tactics leading to false confessions
Reliance on confessions over contradictory evidence (like DNA)
Difficulty in overturning convictions based on confessions
policy_recommendations_raw: Implied need for reforms in police interrogation practices (e.g., recording interrogations, time limits, special protections for juveniles)
Better evaluation of confession evidence by prosecutors and courts

external_links_raw.description: CBS News article on the segment

featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Terrill Swift, part of the "Englewood Four", was wrongfully convicted of rape and murder in Chicago. He was exonerated in 2012 after serving approximately 15 years. His false confession, given as a juvenile after a lengthy interrogation, was a contributing factor.

Jonathan Barr, part of the "Dixmoor Five", was wrongfully convicted of rape and murder in Dixmoor/Chicago. He was exonerated in 2011 after serving approximately 20 years. His coerced/fabricated false confession, given as a juvenile, was a contributing factor.
